Thesis: a group's architecture is sediment of its corporate history, answering 'why is it like this?'
Scope: the timeline from print to break-ups, terms owned, what is left to other chapters
Roadmap of the chapter's sections and its sourcing and labeling rules

Marked two_ideas, but 'What made verticals worth buying also makes their architecture different' ties both halves into the single idea the spec gives p29.
Every unit serves a supporting claim: the waves and their dated record (E1), what each method left (E2), the sediment reading (E3), capital strategy outpacing platforms (E4) and separability (E5).

Each quotation, table and figure is followed or preceded by a sentence saying what it shows; the round-3 gap (Parker's team-size quote) is now explained under 'Minimal, monolithic stacks' ('Simplicity also let small teams run large sites'). Inferences are labeled. A cold reader noted the board table does not say why search gets one cluster set per brand rather than per-brand indexes; this is a depth point, not unexplained evidence.

At every boundary the opening sentence or bolded lead phrase expresses the declared relationship and picks up the carried-over item (e.g. p20 'The record does show' = contrast; p44 'The break-up also reached' = elaboration; p46 'did not disappear' = contrast; p55 'Ingrid's decisions rest on choices every group faces' = cause_effect; p75 summary opening); the closing units link to [[business-capabilities]].

The cold reader predicted the sections in the roadmap's order (Veldmark by year, terms, dated timeline, the four wave sections each with record then what it did to the systems, the sediment reading, Veldmark read that way, trade-offs, vertical differences, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions) and the evidence (dated sourced statements, flagged thin records, labeled inferences, fictional Veldmark), matching 'expected'.

The cold reader gave the expected answer: build search separable from the first design review, one cluster set per brand with indexes rebuildable from the brand-keyed event stream, tenant-scoped data, per-brand accounts and cost centres, exportable contracts, a tested exit path and a EUR 38 million case that survives the sale of any one brand, grounded in Adevinta's costly decentralization and the synergy-to-separation-cost reversal.
